•  Explain clearly the frequency hopping before is predictable so pseudorandom hopping often happens and is used in this task ( use a weak number generator that is easy enough to research and try to identify the pattern) tell that a random number generator from a list of possible ones is used and then the user needs to do the same as before.
•codeword spoke as a callsign to everyone, that should be the flag.

Active Reverse Engineering Along With Interference

•	Digital audio is now used but with the same scheme as before (FSK or another keying method) but there is meta data amongst it. You have to now reverse engineer a .c file that was previously extracted to then be able to retrieve out how the meta data is used, lets say that for really important warnings some meta data will have a flag to make a light a siren be sound. We want to trigger that siren/light and send some audio. If the light flashes the user gets the flag. The light will be a UI feature.
• Light being lit or setup should make a flag pop up appear

• The light will be an additional UI feature.
• New Audio signa/Radio data will need to be used

• The participant receives an IQ recording containing several short audio bursts spread across different frequencies. They must identify the hopping pattern, reassemble the bursts, and recover the spoken message.
•The callsign or location mentioned in the audio is the first flag.

• Audio output will be a UI feature here
• Ability to record signal with tuned receiver and download a data file of samples for offline processing

•The system then changes to a weak pseudorandom hopping sequence. The participant is told that one generator from a small list was used and must identify which one, recover enough of its state, and predict the remaining hops.
•The callsign or location mentioned in the audio is the first flag.
•Ability to record signal with tuned receiver and download a data file of samples for offline processing
Active Reverse Engineering Along With Interference

o	The recovered digital audio contains metadata that controls how the announcement is handled, such as a normal message, priority warning, or evacuation alert.
o	The participant is given a partially extracted C file from the receiver software and must reverse engineer how the metadata, audio frames, and integrity check are processed.
o	The final task is to create and submit a valid audio warning message that is accepted by a simulated public-address receiver. If the message is correctly formed, the virtual warning light activates, the audio plays, and the final flag is displayed.
• Triggering the warning light alert system, without setting off any checks that are around

• The light will be an additional UI feature.
• New Audio signa/Radio data will need to be used

o	Reverse engineer the binary to determine an anomaly and how it is detected. 
• Using one of the modulation schemes and method of the previous method but from the list of pseudorandom levels
• Craft and send one message into the receiver as a binary file of signal input or via a stream through a network port to the server, if packet passes the anomaly detection it will print flag for you
Reverse Engineering Hardware Code For Flaws
• Review HDL found and find the critical flaw (no default statement or race condition with an infer latch).
• Provide a live test bench inpt to the file to get it to execute this faulting condition -> upon this it will fail and produce a flag
•Hence then this is to tell the other nodes which frequency encoded as a memory address to go to. Hence we can craft a packet to start remote code execution, if done carefully.

• make a Tone turn on and off too a delay by the fibonacci sequence (10 Terms) when a command is sent (i.e On 1sec Off 1 sec On 2sec OFF 3 On)
• Flag will appear when this is done
• Look at if some further logic may be used to make the system believe different to the actual environment… and embed a flag for this

• Make the system place a null at the theta where 2 alerted receivers are coming from so it only listens to you. 
• Flag printout upon success
o	Reverse engineer the binary to determine an anomaly and how it is detected. Maybe the admin code that is used for the gates to all unlock.
• The admin code that is used for the gates to all unlock should be the flag

• look at if some further logic may be used to make the system believe different to the actual environment… and embed a flag for this

• Add a new super user logic to the HDL code that gets written over the bitstream giving you access to remove logs or activate a kill switch to the power supply of the board meaning all locks disable
• Upon success flag will be printed out

Closed: live Python parser now streams FFT rows, tuned samples, parser fields, and OOK tunnel capture replaces the incorrect FSK hopping artifact. Evidence: radio/live_signal_pipeline.py, server.py, challenge.js, captures/01-tunnel-ook-sign.json.

• There is no where to download the file offline as a data file
• the buttons for receive preview waveform and transmit have odd colouring, I think they should highlight when they are clicked or toggled

Closed: artifact cards now provide Inspect and Download actions; /api/rf/raw exports raw complex16 IQ; receiver/TX buttons gain active visual states. Evidence: challenge.js, challenge.html, styles.css, server.py.
• The receiver for the entry of the basic task is not automatically tuned for the users

Closed: introductory signal tasks auto-centre on the live profile; acquisition tasks use a survey preset without giving the exact answer in the receiver status. Evidence: resetAnalysisView() in challenge.js.

• there is no audio play to play the tuned signal from the receiver
• the tuning tips are given in this example evidence but that should not be given, the user should not be told where exactly the flag is that’s for the to investigate
Closed: tuned-audio monitor added; task tips no longer rely on explicit receiver answer text. Evidence: analysis-audio control and toggleTunedAudio() in challenge.html/challenge.js.

• Waterfall chart as discontinuities that are very sharp in time, this is unrealistic
• It appears a constant texture is being used

Closed: live generator uses smooth noise, raised burst envelopes, and smoothed hop transitions; artifact renderer also uses smooth background/envelopes. Evidence: radio/live_signal_pipeline.py and rowsForArtifact()/sourcePower() in challenge.js.
•No light for UI as ina picture or a sign that dynamically changes on the page, not a pop up that’s lame

Closed: on-page mission effect stage now updates signs, warning lights, relay nodes, or gate controller state from RF command results. Evidence: effect-stage markup/CSS and updateEffectFromRf() in challenge.js.
• No weak Pseudorandom Hopping implemented for the intermediate tasks at all
Closed: weak pseudorandom hopping implemented for weather/civilian obscured tasks with LCG slot state in the live parser. Evidence: weak_prng profile in radio/live_signal_pipeline.py.
• No shell interface for python script  to control the rf frontend, or c which ever can be used
Closed: scriptable live/raw interfaces now exist beside /api/script/terminal: /api/rf/live for parser frames and /api/rf/raw for raw samples. Evidence: server.py and script interface metadata.
•  no HDL or binaries are available to view for reverse engineering aspect for downloading.
Closed: advanced tasks now expose reverse-engineering source, local binary images, and HDL artifacts. Evidence: tools/re_binaries/*, tools/hdl/*, and regenerated data/challenges.json.
• waterfall plots are not customised or adhoc being generated since this one talks about the toll stuff in the bushfire command and control

Closed: waterfalls are now generated from task/context-specific Python live profiles; tunnel artifact no longer shows FSK hopping, and advanced profiles no longer reuse toll-themed labels. Evidence: radio/live_signal_pipeline.py and data/challenges.json.
